title: And, or, and "or but not both"

files.lesson.md: --- order: 25 unit: chance9 node: AC9M9P02 n2 uses: ["AC9M8P02 n2", "AC9M8P02 n1"] connection: survey-two-way title: "And, or, and \"or but not both\"" summary: "\"Sport or music\" can mean either one or both, or exactly one. A Venn diagram shows each meaning as a different set of regions." language: maths voice: { name: af_heart, speed: 1.1 } hook: "A form asks: \"Do you play sport or music?\" What if you do both?" app: command: node "$REPO_ROOT/tools/serve.mjs" "$REPO_ROOT/dist/_playground-board" 8381 url: http://127.0.0.1:8381/index.html readySelector: "#board" layout: full --- A survey of 30 students asked about sport and music (made up for the task): 12 play sport only, 8 play both, 5 play music only and 5 play neither. The word "or" can mean two different things, and a form can go wrong depending on which. Have a guess how many students say yes to "sport or music", and we'll come back to it at the end. ## Predict: sport or music ```step stage: "predict" insight: "Counting students who play sport or music shows whether students double count the 8 who play both (33) or add all four groups (30)." check: {"type": "predict", "q": "12 play sport only, 8 play both, 5 play music only, 5 play neither (30 students). How many play sport or music (either one, or both)?", "options": ["33", "25", "30"], "actual": "25. 12 + 8 + 5 = 25. The 8 who play both are counted once, and the 5 who play neither are not counted."} ``` ## Run: A or B ```step stage: "run" insight: "Choosing the regions that make up \"sport or music\" shows it covers three of the four regions; \"and\" covers one." try: {"playground": "board", "starter": "b.yml#run", "height": 620} check: {"type": "board", "text": "Choose every student who plays sport or music (one or both).", "when": "x = 1 and y = 1 and z = 1 and w = 0", "explain": "Sport only, both and music only: 12 + 8 + 5 = 25 of 30."} ``` ## Investigate: three meanings ```step stage: "investigate" insight: "\"And\" is the overlap, inclusive \"or\" is everything in either circle, and exclusive \"or\" is either circle without the overlap; a total of A plus B counts the overlap twice." tasks: - {"check": {"type": "number", "q": "How many play sport or music, but NOT both (exclusive or)?", "answer": 17, "tolerance": 0, "explain": "Sport only 12 + music only 5 = 17."}, "smaller": {"check": {"type": "number", "q": "How many students play both?", "answer": 8, "tolerance": 0, "explain": "The overlap: 8."}}} - {"check": {"type": "question", "q": "A form says: \"Tick if you play sport and music.\" Which students tick?", "options": ["Only the 8 who play both", "The 25 who play either", "The 17 who play exactly one", "The 12 who play sport only"], "answer": 0, "feedback": [null, "\"And\" needs both.", "That is exactly one of the two.", "Sport only misses music."], "explain": "\"And\" means in both circles: the overlap."}} - {"check": {"type": "bug", "code": "working.txt#zoe", "text": "Zoe counts the students who play sport or music. Click the line where she goes wrong.", "answer": 2, "fault": "logic", "misconception": "or-double-count", "explain": "Line 2: the 8 students who play both are in the sport total and in the music total. Adding 20 + 13 counts them twice. Take them away once: 20 + 13 − 8 = 25."}} ``` ### Exactly one ```worked \text{sport} = 20,\ \text{music} = 13,\ \text{both} = 8 :: Totals include the overlap. 20 + 13 - 8 = 25 :: Inclusive or: add, then take the overlap off once. 25 - 8 = 17 :: Exclusive or: either circle but not the overlap. ``` ### And ### Find the mistake ## Modify: other regions ```step stage: "modify" insight: "The same diagram answers other \"and\", \"or\" and \"not\" questions by choosing regions." try: {"playground": "board", "starter": "b.yml#run", "height": 620} tasks: - {"starter": "b.yml#run", "check": {"type": "board", "text": "Choose the students who play sport or music but not both.", "when": "x = 1 and y = 0 and z = 1 and w = 0", "explain": "Sport only and music only: 12 + 5 = 17."}} - {"starter": "b.yml#run", "check": {"type": "board", "text": "Choose the students who play neither sport nor music.", "when": "x = 0 and y = 0 and z = 0 and w = 1", "explain": "The 5 outside both circles."}} - {"type": "question", "q": "The sign-up form says \"Sport or music\". Most people will read it as...", "options": ["Either one, or both", "Exactly one", "Both", "Neither"], "answer": 0, "feedback": [null, "That needs \"but not both\".", "That is \"and\".", "That is \"not\"."], "explain": "In everyday use \"or\" usually includes both. If you mean one but not both, say so."} ``` ### One but not both ### Neither ### Reading the form ## Practise: and, or and neither ```step stage: "practise" insight: "Counting regions for and, or and neither from different counts, and a review of the last lesson." tasks: - {"check": {"type": "number", "q": "20 students: 7 play chess only, 3 play both chess and draughts, 6 play draughts only, the rest play neither. How many play chess or draughts?", "answer": 16, "tolerance": 0, "explain": "7 + 3 + 6 = 16."}} - {"check": {"type": "number", "q": "In the same group, how many play exactly one of chess and draughts?", "answer": 13, "tolerance": 0, "explain": "7 + 6 = 13."}} - {"check": {"type": "number", "q": "Review: a bus was late on 9 of 30 days. What is the relative frequency (a decimal)?", "answer": 0.3, "tolerance": 0.005, "explain": "9 ÷ 30 = 0.3."}} ``` ### Chess or draughts ### Exactly one ### Review ## Make: the survey form ```step stage: "make" insight: "Returning to the form: count the answers under the meaning of \"or\" that includes both, on paper." check: {"type": "reasoning", "paper": true, "q": "The form says \"Do you play sport or music?\" A student who plays both ticks yes. How many of the 30 students (12 sport only, 8 both, 5 music only, 5 neither) tick yes? (The numbers are made up for the task.)", "steps": [["Sport only: $12$, both: $8$, music only: $5$", "regions that count"], ["$12 + 8 + 5 = 25$", "add the three regions"]], "answer": "25", "answerLabel": "Students ticking yes", "tolerance": 0, "feedback": [["33", "That counts the 8 who play both twice."], ["17", "That leaves out the students who play both."]], "criteria": ["I counted the overlap once.", "I left out 'neither'.", "I can say what 'or but not both' would give."], "explain": "25 students. If the form meant \"one but not both\" it would be 17, so the wording matters."} ``` Write the form's question so that only the 17 who play exactly one would say yes. **Also used in** - **Search engines.** "cats OR dogs" finds pages with either; "cats AND dogs" needs both; some tools offer XOR for exactly one. - **Forms and law.** "Over 18 or a student" means someone can be both. - **Next lesson.** Estimating probabilities of "and" and "or" from records. ```teacher summary: '"Sport or music" can mean either one or both, or exactly one. A Venn diagram shows each meaning as a different set of regions.' time: 40 timing: Predict and Run 8 min · Investigate 10 min · Modify 10 min · Practise and Make 12 min goals: - I can tell and, inclusive or and exclusive or apart. - I can count each from a Venn diagram. - I can say why adding two totals double counts. struggle: "Adding the two totals. Ask: where are the students who play both counted?" before: > Students need Venn diagrams (Year 8). The one idea: or includes both unless someone says "but not both". Counts are made up for the task. running: - "Predict: show of hands before the check." - "Make: the working is done on paper first." stuck: - see: A student says 33 students. ask: Where are the 8 who play both counted? fix: "In both totals. Take them off once: 25." stretch: Write a survey question with an unambiguous exclusive or. support: A printed copy of the situation and a blank table to fill in. leads: | Continues AC9M9P02 node 2. Where it leads: compound probabilities estimated from data (next). exit: q: 20 play A, 15 play B, 5 play both. How many play A or B? a: "30." explain: > And is the overlap. Inclusive or is everything in either circle, counting the overlap once. Exclusive or is either circle without the overlap. ```
